_readme: THE RUNG MANIFEST — the single authority on what a rung is.
A rung is an entry in this file. Not a path convention, not a directory, not a naming
convention. Path conventions were tried and failed: a close condition that matched a path
STRING went green with nine rung files still shipping. A string can be satisfied by a tree
that violates the property; a manifest gives you a SET with a declared cardinality, which
is the thing an exact-count assertion can be written against.
TWO FACETS, DELIBERATELY SEPARATE. They answer different questions and must not be conflated:
owns[]   — WHICH FILES DIE when a lower rung is ejected.   (severability / `pnpm eject`)
target   — WHERE THE SHELL SENDS YOU for this rung.        (routing / the shape-routed shell)
A rung's files and a rung's entry point are not the same thing: rungs 1-3 own files in two
language planes but share ONE surface, and rung 4 owns a whole app served from another origin.
OWNERSHIP IS TOTAL AND DISJOINT. Every tracked file is owned by exactly one rung or matched
by `shared`. A file matching neither is a hard CI failure, and `shared` is an enumerated
allowlist rather than a fallback — otherwise 'forgot to classify' becomes the way to pass.
NOT IN SCOPE, ON PURPOSE — do not add these: stream topology, threadId/runId, endpoint URLs,
graph names, or anything describing how a run is carried. `shape` declares the interaction
kind and the shape handler owns everything downstream of that. Rung 4 is the reason: real
Open SWE registers three graphs that do NOT share a run, so any per-rung `threadId` or single
stream endpoint would bake in a topology that is already known to be wrong. See
apps/open-swe/docs/LOCAL-AGENT.md 'Topology: this backend is single-run'.

states.implemented: Present in this repo and runnable from a clean fork.
states.external-required: Present, but needs a service or account this repo cannot provide.
states.planned: Declared in the ladder, not present in the repo. MUST own no ts/py source files (C5 in scripts/classify.mjs enforces exactly this). It MAY own docs -- the ladder documents a rung before it exists -- so ownedFileCount is not required to be 0. Earlier wording here said it must be 0, which C5 never checked and rung 5 never satisfied while planned (it owned its guide).

_note: REACHABILITY IS A SECOND AXIS, NOT A STATE VALUE (#424).
`state` answers IS THIS RUNG HERE AND RUNNABLE. `reach` answers DOES IT HAVE A FRONT
DOOR. They are independent: a rung can be present and runnable with no way in, which is
rung 5 today, and that combination is the whole sentence v2.0 ships — five forkable,
four reachable. One field could not say it: `implemented` was true of rung 4 and rung 5
alike, and `implemented` + `target.kind:"none"` was a legal combination nothing objected
to.
WHY NOT FOLD THIS INTO `state`, which was the first proposal. Measured: THREE call sites
read `state` today and ALL THREE want presence -- defaultChatId() in apps/open-swe
("really here"), adapters/registry.test.ts ("really here"), and the dashboard tile
labelled "Implemented / runnable from a clean fork". ZERO read reachability. Replacing
`implemented` with `referenced`/`vendored` would make every one of them enumerate two
values to ask one question, and would make that dashboard tile count ZERO. Folding a
second fact into the field would repeat, one value over, the defect this change removes.
SCOPED TO THIS TREE, DELIBERATELY. `referenced` means the front door is DECLARED AND
PRESENT HERE. It does not mean the door answers in your deployment: rung 4's origin comes
from NEXT_PUBLIC_QUEUE_URL, so whether it serves is per-deployment and no static field can
carry it. The manifest already has the slot for that axis -- `state:"external-required"`
means a service this repo cannot provide -- and rung 4 is `implemented` precisely because
its localhost fallback makes it runnable from a clean fork.
reaches.referenced: Present AND has a front door in this tree: a target that is not `none`, resolving to a real route. Rungs 1-4.
reaches.vendored: Present and severable, and NO front door: `target.kind` is `none`, and nothing this rung emits is mounted by any app. Rung 5.

_note: Rung-agnostic paths. An ENUMERATED ALLOWLIST, never a fallback: adding to it is a
deliberate, reviewable edit, so a rung file cannot become 'shared' by being forgotten.
packages/{edge,remix,sveltekit} are here because they are HOST-FRAMEWORK PORTS on an axis
orthogonal to the ladder — each hardcodes no adapter and takes one as a caller option
(edge/src/types.ts, sveltekit/src/handler.ts, remix/src/handler.ts all say so). An ejected
repo at any rung keeps every framework port.
apps/open-swe/** IS HERE AS OF #154, AND IT IS THE SAME KIND OF ENTRY AS apps/example/**.
It is the PRODUCT'S app, not rung 4's app. The shell, the theme, conversation history, the
chat at / and /settings are how the product looks at EVERY rung — while the whole directory
was rung-4-owned, a fork of rungs 1-3 deleted all of it, so improving the product meant
improving the one app most forks do not get. Rung 4 now owns the RUN SURFACE inside this
app — /runs, /api/open-swe, the agent server, the sandbox and the run domain model — file by
file, exactly as rungs 1-3 own individual files inside apps/example/**. Partial ownership of
a shared app is the pattern this repo already uses, not a new one.
_censusNote: MEMBERSHIP OF TWO OF THESE GLOBS IS FROZEN. See scripts/shared-census.json.
A glob records intent; the classifier consumes it per FILE. `packages/server/**` is one
deliberate line covering ~65 files, and the membership of any GIVEN file was decided by
nobody. attribution.pipeline.test.ts arrived in #45 with no manifest edit, matched that
glob, and sat in `shared` for 29 commits until #57 claimed it. `pnpm eject` exited FAIL on
main throughout. The census fires on the commit that introduces such a file.
FROZEN:     packages/server/** and packages/react/**
NOT FROZEN: the other 21 globs. A MEASURED REFUSAL, not an oversight or an omission.
Measured over 61 commits, initial import excluded:
all 23 globs      760 files   32/61 commits (52%) would need a census edit;
28 of those by an author not already editing rungs.json
the 2 frozen       96 files    8/61 (13%), of which 7 (11%) are added friction
the other 21      498 files   22/61 (36%), of which 19 (31%) are added friction
The cost and the value are in DIFFERENT globs. Every misclassification in this repo's
history landed in the two frozen ones; the other 498 files have produced none. Freezing
everything means a manifest edit on roughly one commit in two, and a freeze edited that
often gets rubber-stamped -- worse than no freeze, because it reads as review.
REVISIT WHEN either becomes true, and re-measure with the same method rather than
arguing from memory:
1. a misclassification is found in a glob that is not frozen -- the premise above was
that none ever has been, and one instance falsifies it;
2. an unfrozen glob's membership stops churning, which makes freezing it nearly free.
.planning/** is 374 of the 760 files and moved once in 61 commits; it is excluded for
being planning prose, not for being expensive.
_sharedExceptions: The globs above are evaluated AFTER rung ownership, so a rung-owned file inside a shared
tree (e.g. packages/server/src/adapters/langchain.ts inside packages/server/**) stays owned
by its rung. Rung ownership always wins; `shared` only catches what no rung claimed.
_knownRungNamedNote: C7 flags any shared file whose path segments name a rung, because a broad shared glob can
swallow a rung file silently (docs/rungs/4-open-swe.md under `docs/**` was a real instance).
These entries are the genuine exceptions, and each needs a reason:
apps/django-backend/deepagents_backend/** — `deepagents_backend` is the DJANGO PROJECT
package name, not the deepagents rung. The rung's file inside it (ai_backends/deepagents.py)
is claimed by rung 3's `owns` and so never reaches this allowlist.
apps/fastapi-backend/** — its ai_backends/ package is named for the rung axis generally;
the per-rung modules inside are individually rung-owned.
apps/open-swe/** — the DIRECTORY is named for rung 4 because the app was born as rung 4's
app. #154 ended that: it is the product's app now, hosting rung 4's run surface among
other things, so every shared file under it has `open-swe` in its path and C7 fires on
all 68 of them. The run-surface files inside are individually claimed by rung 4's `owns`,
so they never reach this allowlist.
ONE entry rather than many, and the cost is real and worth naming: C7 no longer guards
this directory. A NEW run-surface file added under apps/open-swe/lib/ and not written
into rung 4's `owns` is absorbed as shared instead of flagged. What catches it instead is
`pnpm eject` — a shared file that reaches a rung-owned one fails the dangling-import
guard and then the fork's build — which is weaker, because it only fires when the
misfiled file HAPPENS to import something that left. Grouping the run surface under one
directory rung 4 could own by glob would restore the guard; that is a move, not a
manifest edit, and it is not in this change.
Adding a line here is a deliberate, reviewable act. That is the point: a rung file cannot
become 'shared' by being forgotten, only by someone writing it down.
_rendererNote: DEV7 found nine rung-named renderers in packages/react classified as shared, and was right
that it was wrong. Applying TEAMLEAD's rule -- assign to the LOWEST rung that EMITS the
payload, since higher rungs inherit through `requires` -- per card rather than as a block:
rung 3 (deepagentsEnrich emits): TodoCard data-todo, FileCard data-file,
SubAgentCard data-sub-agent. FileCard and SubAgentCard are emitted by BOTH
enrichers; rung 3 is the lower, and rung 4 inherits them via requires.
rung 4 (openSweEnrich ONLY):     PlanCard data-plan, and PlanProgress, which renders
inside PlanCard and so moves with it.
Also `data-approval` (#492) -- the BARE part, emitted only by openSweEnrich, and
NOT `data-approval-required`, which is core's and stays inline. It is rendered by
ApprovalCard, which remains SHARED: OWNERSHIP IS PER PART TYPE, NOT PER CARD, and
a shared component may render a rung-owned part. Reasoning per card is what left
an inline branch for it in two shared surfaces while its emitter was pruned, so
every fork below rung 4 shipped a renderer for a frame it could never receive.
SHARED, and moving them would have been a BUG: ApprovalCard consumes
data-approval-required and HumanResponseCard data-human-response, both emitted by
approval-gating.ts -- which #30 moved into CORE. Filing them under a rung would
make `eject langgraph` delete the UI for a CORE feature.
useApprovalCardController serves ApprovalCard and follows it.
SHARED, but flagged: TaskCard (data-task) and AgentsMdCard (data-agents-md) have NO
emitter anywhere in this repo -- both parts are declared in react/src/schemas.ts
and exercised only by hand-crafted SSE in tests and e2e. A consumer's own backend
may emit them, so they are not dead code in a library; in a reference
implementation they are a contract with no producer. Raised as issue #50, with both resolutions and no recommendation; PRODUCT rules.
_specimenNote: specimen/** — preserved evidence that a checker can fire, kept because the live tree stops
exhibiting the defect once it is fixed (#448, following #406's specimen/stale-tree-reverts-398).
SHARED and not rung-owned: a specimen is about a CHECKER, not about a rung, and it must
survive every eject for the same reason the checker does. It is documentation of a
reproduction, so it owns no source and an ejected fork carries it harmlessly.

_topologyNote: TOPOLOGIES ARE PER (RUNG, RUNTIME), NEVER PER RUNG. The ladder has exactly one ragged cell:
deep-research exists only in deepagents x fastapi -- verified by reading TOPOLOGIES in all six
ai_backends modules. A rung-level topologies[] array cannot express that: it would either emit
a django x deep-research cell that 404s, or silently drop fastapi's real one.
`topologies: []` means ONE CELL WITH NO TOPOLOGY AXIS -- not zero cells. `run` rungs have no
topology axis, and if empty collapsed to zero they would vanish from the matrix silently.
Rather than leave that to be re-derived by each of the three consumers, rungs.generated.ts
EXPORTS matrixCells(): a semantic that can be guessed wrong should be a function, not a comment.
`runtimes` is NOT `languages`. languages = which language planes hold FILES this rung owns, and
drives the severability eject matrix. runtimes = which backends SERVE this rung, and drives the
behavioural matrix. Rung 1 has languages [ts, py] (it owns a TS adapter AND two Python modules)
but runtimes [django, fastapi] (no node runtime serves it). They are close enough to be
conflated and different enough that conflating them would be wrong.
_ownershipCouplingNote: ADDING A PRODUCER AND CLAIMING ITS FILE ARE COUPLED. `shared.paths` includes
`packages/server/**`, so a new adapter there is absorbed as shared rather than
flagged as unclassified -- nothing objects to it. But the #59 frame-attribution
test derives a tag to "core" if ANY of its producers is unowned, so a new emitter
that has not yet been claimed in some rung's `owns.ts` will drag every tag it
emits to "core" and fail. That is correct by default (an unclaimed file IS
